eras.name: Golden Age
eras.description: The dawn of Timely Comics. Marvel's ancestor publisher launched with Marvel Comics #1, introducing the original Human Torch and Namor the Sub-Mariner. Wartime patriotism drove the debut of Captain America.

milestones.title: Timely Comics founded
milestones.description: Martin Goodman launches Timely Publications, the company that will eventually become Marvel Comics.

milestones.title: Marvel Comics #1 published
milestones.description: First issue debuts the original android Human Torch (Carl Burgos) and Namor the Sub-Mariner (Bill Everett). Cover-dated October 1939.

milestones.title: Namor gets his own title
milestones.description: Sub-Mariner Comics #1 launches, making Namor one of the earliest superhero solo stars and comics' first antihero.

milestones.title: Captain America Comics #1
milestones.description: Joe Simon and Jack Kirby debut Captain America punching Adolf Hitler on the cover, months before U.S. entry into WWII. Sells nearly a million copies.

milestones.title: Stan Lee joins Timely
milestones.description: Stanley Martin Lieber hired as an office assistant at age 17; publishes his first text filler in Captain America Comics #3.

milestones.title: The All-Winners Squad forms
milestones.description: Timely's first superhero team-up, uniting Captain America, Human Torch, Sub-Mariner, Whizzer, and Miss America, debuts in All Winners Comics #1.

milestones.title: Superhero line collapses
milestones.description: Post-war demand for capes evaporates. Captain America Comics ends its original run; Timely pivots hard toward genre anthologies.

eras.name: Atlas Era
eras.description: Timely rebranded as Atlas Comics under Martin Goodman. Superhero sales collapsed post-war; the publisher pivoted to monster, horror, western, war, and romance anthologies that trained the artists who would define the next era.

milestones.title: Atlas Comics branding adopted
milestones.description: Goodman rebrands Timely as Atlas Comics, standardizing the globe logo across a sprawling anthology line.

milestones.title: Journey into Mystery debuts
milestones.description: Anthology launches as a horror/suspense title. It will later host the debut of Thor.

milestones.title: Comics Code Authority created
milestones.description: In response to Wertham's Seduction of the Innocent, publishers self-impose the CCA. Atlas's horror and crime titles are gutted overnight.

milestones.title: Atlas Implosion
milestones.description: Goodman's distribution deal with American News collapses. Atlas fires most of its staff and shrinks output from ~85 titles/month to a handful.

milestones.title: Tales to Astonish launches
milestones.description: Monster anthology debuts; will later become the home of Ant-Man and Hulk.

milestones.title: Groot debuts
milestones.description: The original Groot appears in Tales to Astonish #13 as a Kirby-drawn alien invader — decades before his Guardians of the Galaxy revival.

eras.name: Silver Age
eras.description: The Marvel Universe as we know it was born. Fantastic Four #1 kicked off a rapid-fire debut run — Spider-Man, X-Men, Hulk, Iron Man, Thor, Daredevil, Doctor Strange, Black Panther — anchored by flawed, human characters and a shared continuity.

milestones.title: Fantastic Four #1
milestones.description: Stan Lee and Jack Kirby launch the Marvel Age. Reed, Sue, Johnny, and Ben get powers from cosmic rays; unlike DC heroes, they fight, worry about rent, and don't wear masks.

milestones.title: Hulk debuts
milestones.description: Incredible Hulk #1 introduces Bruce Banner, a scientist transformed by a gamma-bomb blast into a raging monster — Marvel's Jekyll and Hyde.

milestones.title: Spider-Man debuts
milestones.description: Amazing Fantasy #15 introduces Peter Parker in a 'try-out' issue that becomes a smash. Lee and Ditko invent the flawed teen hero.

milestones.title: Thor debuts
milestones.description: Journey into Mystery #83 introduces Dr. Don Blake and his hammer Mjolnir. Kirby's Norse-mythology aesthetic reshapes Marvel's cosmic side.

milestones.title: Ant-Man debuts as a hero
milestones.description: Tales to Astonish #35 gives Hank Pym his costume; Wasp joins in issue #44 (1963).

milestones.title: Iron Man debuts
milestones.description: Tales of Suspense #39 introduces Tony Stark, wounded weapons manufacturer who builds armor to escape captivity — Lee's deliberate attempt to make readers root for a millionaire arms dealer.

milestones.title: Doctor Strange debuts
milestones.description: Strange Tales #110 introduces Ditko's Sorcerer Supreme, opening up Marvel's mystical dimensions.

milestones.title: Avengers assemble
milestones.description: Avengers #1 unites Thor, Iron Man, Hulk, Ant-Man, and Wasp. Captain America joins in issue #4 (1964), thawed from Arctic ice.

milestones.title: X-Men debut
milestones.description: X-Men #1 introduces Professor Xavier's teenage students Cyclops, Marvel Girl, Beast, Iceman, and Angel — plus Magneto.

milestones.title: Daredevil debuts
milestones.description: Daredevil #1 introduces blind lawyer Matt Murdock, laying groundwork for Marvel's street-level tier.

milestones.title: Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. launches
milestones.description: Strange Tales #135 debuts S.H.I.E.L.D. and pivots WWII vet Nick Fury into Marvel's answer to James Bond.

milestones.title: Black Panther debuts
milestones.description: Fantastic Four #52 introduces T'Challa, king of Wakanda — the first Black superhero in mainstream American comics.

milestones.title: Galactus and Silver Surfer arrive
milestones.description: The Galactus Trilogy (FF #48–50) introduces the world-eater and his herald, expanding Marvel's cosmic scale.

milestones.title: Captain Marvel debuts
milestones.description: Marvel Super-Heroes #12 introduces the Kree warrior Mar-Vell, securing the 'Captain Marvel' trademark Marvel had lost to Fawcett/DC.

milestones.title: Falcon debuts
milestones.description: Captain America #117 introduces Sam Wilson, Marvel's first African-American superhero (Black Panther is African).

eras.name: Bronze Age
eras.description: Marvel matured. Stories tackled drug abuse, racism, and social upheaval. The Comics Code weakened, Wolverine debuted, the Phoenix Saga redefined tragedy, and street-level heroes like Punisher entered the roster.

milestones.title: Spider-Man drug issues break the Code
milestones.description: Amazing Spider-Man #96–98 publish an anti-drug story WITHOUT Comics Code approval at the U.S. government's request. The CCA revises its rules the same year.

milestones.title: Conan the Barbarian launches
milestones.description: Roy Thomas adapts Robert E. Howard's character; the title makes sword-and-sorcery a Marvel staple.

milestones.title: Luke Cage: Hero for Hire #1
milestones.description: Marvel's first Black character to headline his own title, riding the blaxploitation wave.

milestones.title: Ghost Rider debuts
milestones.description: Marvel Spotlight #5 introduces Johnny Blaze, a stunt rider bonded to the demon Zarathos.

milestones.title: Death of Gwen Stacy
milestones.description: Amazing Spider-Man #121 kills Gwen when the Green Goblin throws her off a bridge. Considered the end of the Silver Age of comics.

milestones.title: Punisher debuts
milestones.description: Amazing Spider-Man #129 introduces Frank Castle, initially a villain. Wolverine also debuts this year in Incredible Hulk #180–181.

milestones.title: Giant-Size X-Men #1
milestones.description: Len Wein and Dave Cockrum relaunch the team with Storm, Nightcrawler, Colossus, and Wolverine. Chris Claremont takes over the writing with issue #94.

milestones.title: Star Wars #1
milestones.description: Marvel's Star Wars adaptation reportedly saves the company from bankruptcy during a rough period for the industry.

milestones.title: Dark Phoenix Saga concludes
milestones.description: X-Men #137 kills Jean Grey after the Phoenix Force consumes a star system. Claremont/Byrne redefine what mainstream superhero tragedy can look like.

milestones.title: Days of Future Past
milestones.description: X-Men #141–142 depict a dystopian future ruled by Sentinels. Template for countless time-travel stories in comics and film.

milestones.title: Wolverine limited series
milestones.description: Claremont and Frank Miller's four-issue series establishes Logan's samurai code and Japanese-honor storyline.

milestones.title: Death of Elektra
milestones.description: Daredevil #181 has Bullseye murder Elektra with her own sai; one of Frank Miller's defining runs.

milestones.title: New Mutants and mutant expansion
milestones.description: The X-line branches with The New Mutants (1983) and Alpha Flight (1983), starting the mutant franchise sprawl.

eras.name: Modern Age
eras.description: Line-wide crossovers became the engine — Secret Wars, Mutant Massacre, Inferno, Infinity Gauntlet. Todd McFarlane, Jim Lee, and Rob Liefeld drove the art boom that ended with the founders leaving to start Image Comics in 1992.

milestones.title: Secret Wars launches
milestones.description: Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars #1 kicks off the first line-wide crossover event, driven by a Mattel toy tie-in. Spider-Man returns wearing the black suit — the future Venom symbiote.

milestones.title: Mutant Massacre
milestones.description: The Marauders slaughter the Morlocks in a crossover through Uncanny X-Men, X-Factor, New Mutants, Thor, and Power Pack.

milestones.title: Venom debuts as a villain
milestones.description: Amazing Spider-Man #300 introduces Eddie Brock bonded to the alien symbiote, drawn by Todd McFarlane.

milestones.title: Inferno crossover
milestones.description: N'astirh's demons invade Manhattan; the X-line's biggest crossover to date.

milestones.title: Death of Robin (DC)
milestones.description: Though a DC event, the phone-in Death of Jason Todd shifts industry appetite toward shock deaths — a trend Marvel adopts through the Modern Age.

milestones.title: Spider-Man #1 by McFarlane
milestones.description: Adjectiveless Spider-Man #1 sells 2.5 million copies with variant covers, launching the collector's speculation boom.

milestones.title: Cable debuts
milestones.description: New Mutants #87 introduces Rob Liefeld's Cable, the time-traveling son of Cyclops and Madelyne Pryor.

milestones.title: X-Men #1 by Jim Lee
milestones.description: Jim Lee's X-Men #1 sells over 8 million copies with five variant covers — the best-selling comic of all time.

milestones.title: Infinity Gauntlet event
milestones.description: Jim Starlin and George Pérez's six-issue miniseries has Thanos snap away half of all life. Blueprint for the eventual MCU adaptation 27 years later.

milestones.title: Deadpool debuts
milestones.description: New Mutants #98 introduces Wade Wilson, initially a straight villain-for-hire before Joe Kelly makes him the fourth-wall breaker.

milestones.title: Image Comics exodus
milestones.description: McFarlane, Lee, Liefeld, Silvestri, Portacio, Larsen, and Valentino leave Marvel to found Image Comics. The event ends Marvel's art-boom dominance.

eras.name: Dark Age
eras.description: The speculator bubble burst. Marvel filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 1996. Heroes Reborn outsourced flagship titles to former Marvel artists; the Onslaught event reset the board. The company clawed back to solvency by decade's end.

milestones.title: Age of Apocalypse
milestones.description: An alternate-reality X-line takeover for four months. Charles Xavier is dead, Magneto leads the X-Men, and Apocalypse rules North America.

milestones.title: Clone Saga peaks
milestones.description: The multi-year Spider-Man storyline, which briefly makes clone Ben Reilly the real Peter Parker, becomes a byword for over-extended editorial mandates.

milestones.title: Onslaught event
milestones.description: Psychic entity forces the Avengers and Fantastic Four to sacrifice themselves, clearing the deck for Heroes Reborn.

milestones.title: Marvel files Chapter 11
milestones.description: December bankruptcy filing after the collector's-bubble collapse and disastrous Marvelution restructuring.

milestones.title: Heroes Reborn launches
milestones.description: Marvel outsources Avengers, Iron Man, Fantastic Four, and Captain America to Jim Lee and Rob Liefeld's Image studios for a full year.

milestones.title: Marvel Knights imprint founded
milestones.description: Joe Quesada and Jimmy Palmiotti's Event Comics gets the contract to relaunch Daredevil, Punisher, Inhumans, and Black Panther, restoring Marvel's critical credibility.

eras.name: Marvel Knights & Ultimate Era
eras.description: Joe Quesada's Marvel Knights imprint restored critical credibility with darker takes on Daredevil, Punisher, and Inhumans. The Ultimate line rebooted continuity for new readers — Ultimate Spider-Man became a runaway hit and blueprinted the eventual MCU.

milestones.title: Ultimate Spider-Man launches
milestones.description: Brian Michael Bendis and Mark Bagley reboot Peter Parker for new readers on the Ultimate imprint. Runs 160+ issues, blueprint for the MCU's tone.

milestones.title: Ultimate X-Men launches
milestones.description: Mark Millar reboots the X-Men in the Ultimate line, contemporary and militarized.

milestones.title: Joe Quesada becomes Editor-in-Chief
milestones.description: Quesada takes over from Bob Harras; ushers in the modern era with the 'no more marriages' edict and creator-driven relaunches.

milestones.title: Ultimates launches
milestones.description: Millar and Bryan Hitch's Ultimate Avengers is designed to look like a movie. Ultimate Nick Fury is explicitly modeled on Samuel L. Jackson — the visual template Marvel Studios would use verbatim.

milestones.title: New X-Men by Grant Morrison
milestones.description: Morrison's three-year run introduces the black leather uniforms, Cassandra Nova, and the 'mutants are the dominant culture' pivot.

milestones.title: Alias #1 debuts Jessica Jones
milestones.description: First title on the mature-readers MAX imprint. Bendis and Michael Gaydos introduce Jessica Jones.

milestones.title: Bendis takes over Daredevil
milestones.description: Following Kevin Smith and David Mack, Bendis and Alex Maleev's 55-issue run outs Matt Murdock's identity and reshapes street-level Marvel.

milestones.title: Runaways debuts
milestones.description: Brian K. Vaughan and Adrian Alphona's teen team about kids discovering their parents are supervillains — a rare hit outside the main line.

eras.name: Event Era
eras.description: Bendis, Millar, and Hickman built Marvel around annual line-wide events. Avengers Disassembled led into House of M, Civil War, Secret Invasion, Dark Reign, Siege, and Fear Itself. Each event permanently altered status quo.

milestones.title: Avengers Disassembled
milestones.description: Bendis kills Ant-Man, Vision, and Hawkeye and dissolves the team. Prologue to the Event Era.

milestones.title: House of M
milestones.description: The Scarlet Witch reshapes reality then reverses it with 'No more mutants,' depowering 90%+ of Earth's mutant population.

milestones.title: New Avengers launches
milestones.description: Bendis reforms the Avengers with Spider-Man, Wolverine, and Luke Cage — the first time these characters are members of the main team.

milestones.title: Return of Bucky as Winter Soldier
milestones.description: Ed Brubaker's Captain America run reveals Bucky Barnes survived WWII as a Soviet assassin. Basis for the MCU film.

milestones.title: Civil War
milestones.description: Mark Millar's seven-issue event splits heroes over the Superhuman Registration Act. Cap and Iron Man on opposing sides.

milestones.title: Death of Captain America
milestones.description: Captain America #25 has Steve Rogers assassinated on the courthouse steps after Civil War. Bucky takes the shield.

milestones.title: One More Day
milestones.description: Peter Parker and Mary Jane's marriage is erased by Mephisto to save Aunt May's life — Quesada's controversial reset of the Spider-Man status quo.

milestones.title: Secret Invasion
milestones.description: Bendis reveals Skrulls have been replacing heroes for years. Ends with Norman Osborn shooting the Skrull Queen on live TV.

milestones.title: Dark Reign begins
milestones.description: Norman Osborn takes over S.H.I.E.L.D. (rebranded H.A.M.M.E.R.) and forms his own Dark Avengers. Year-long villains-in-charge status quo.

milestones.title: Siege ends Dark Reign
milestones.description: Osborn invades Asgard; the Sentry destroys it; Steve Rogers resumes command of the Avengers.

milestones.title: Fear Itself
milestones.description: Matt Fraction event pits Thor and the Avengers against the Serpent, the Asgardian god of fear. Bucky-Cap dies (briefly).

milestones.title: Ultimate Peter Parker dies
milestones.description: In the Ultimate universe, Peter is killed defending his family. Miles Morales debuts in Ultimate Fallout #4.

milestones.title: Avengers vs. X-Men
milestones.description: 12-issue event: the Phoenix Force possesses Cyclops and four X-Men. Ends with Xavier's death and the return of mutants after House of M.

eras.name: MCU Synergy Era
eras.description: The Marvel Cinematic Universe reshaped the comics. Marvel NOW! and All-New All-Different relaunches aligned characters and looks with their film versions. Hickman's Avengers/New Avengers built to Secret Wars (2015), rebooting continuity as the All-New All-Different Marvel.

milestones.title: Marvel NOW! relaunch
milestones.description: Post-AvX line-wide soft reboot. Uncanny Avengers debuts; Hickman takes over Avengers and New Avengers to build the road to Secret Wars.

milestones.title: Superior Spider-Man launches
milestones.description: Doctor Octopus swaps minds with Peter Parker and runs the Spidey title for 33 issues as a 'better' hero.

milestones.title: Hawkeye by Fraction and Aja
milestones.description: Ground-level Hawkeye run introducing Kate Bishop as co-lead. Direct visual inspiration for the MCU Hawkeye series.

milestones.title: Ms. Marvel #1 (Kamala Khan)
milestones.description: G. Willow Wilson introduces Kamala Khan, Marvel's first Muslim character to headline her own title. Runaway critical hit.

milestones.title: Sam Wilson becomes Captain America
milestones.description: Falcon takes the shield after Steve Rogers loses his super-soldier serum in Rick Remender's run.

milestones.title: Jane Foster becomes Thor
milestones.description: Jason Aaron's run has an unworthy Thor Odinson lose Mjolnir; Jane Foster picks it up despite her cancer treatment killing her every time she transforms.

milestones.title: Secret Wars reboots continuity
milestones.description: Hickman's eight-year Avengers plan culminates: the 616 and Ultimate universes collide, Doctor Doom rebuilds a Battleworld, then Reed Richards reboots reality. Launchpad for All-New, All-Different Marvel.

milestones.title: Riri Williams (Ironheart) debuts
milestones.description: Bendis introduces the 15-year-old MIT student who reverse-engineers Iron Man armor. Debuts in Invincible Iron Man #7.

milestones.title: Civil War II
milestones.description: Bendis pits Iron Man against Captain Marvel over predictive justice. Bruce Banner and War Machine die.

milestones.title: Secret Empire
milestones.description: Nick Spencer's controversial event where a cosmic-cube-altered Steve Rogers, now a Hydra sleeper agent, takes over America.

milestones.title: Donny Cates takes over Venom
milestones.description: Cates's run reveals the symbiote's cosmic origins (Knull, the King in Black), reshaping the Marvel cosmic mythology for the next several years.

eras.name: Krakoan Age & Beyond
eras.description: Jonathan Hickman's House of X / Powers of X relaunched the X-Men on the mutant nation-state of Krakoa, reframing the franchise around resurrection, diplomacy, and existential threat. The line closed with Fall of X and transitioned into From the Ashes in 2024.
landmarkIssues: Fall of the House of X #1 (2024)

milestones.title: House of X / Powers of X
milestones.description: Jonathan Hickman and Pepe Larraz's twin miniseries reboot the X-line. Mutants found the sovereign island nation of Krakoa and unlock resurrection.

milestones.title: Dawn of X relaunch
milestones.description: X-Men, Marauders, Excalibur, X-Force, New Mutants, and Fallen Angels relaunch under the Krakoan status quo.

milestones.title: King in Black
milestones.description: Donny Cates and Ryan Stegman's event: Knull, god of the symbiotes, invades Earth.

milestones.title: Hellfire Gala tradition begins
milestones.description: Annual X-line event: mutant fashion gala where a new X-Men roster is elected. Reshapes the year's stories.

milestones.title: Ta-Nehisi Coates ends Captain America run
milestones.description: Concludes his four-year Cap run following his acclaimed Black Panther work.

milestones.title: A.X.E.: Judgment Day
milestones.description: Kieron Gillen's event: the Progenitor, a Celestial made from Uranos, judges every person on Earth by their potential to be good.

milestones.title: Sins of Sinister
milestones.description: Alternate-timeline Krakoan story where Mister Sinister has manipulated the resurrection protocols. Explores 1,000 years of a Sinister-ruled galaxy.

milestones.title: Fall of X begins
milestones.description: Orchis destroys the Hellfire Gala, deactivates the resurrection protocols, and drives mutants underground. Ends the Krakoan era.

milestones.title: Fall of the House of X / Rise of the Powers of X
milestones.description: Kieron Gillen and Al Ewing's twin miniseries close out the Krakoan Age. Krakoa is destroyed; the X-Men splinter.

milestones.title: From the Ashes relaunch
milestones.description: New X-line launches with the X-Men fractured across multiple teams. Cyclops leads one team, Rogue another, Xavier is imprisoned.
